assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a theoretical flat-band prediction into a new, tunable platform for correlated and superconducting phases. It is a discovery found by listening to nature: the phenomena (correlated insulators, superconductivity near the magic angle) were measured, not merely proposed, and a large field followed.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. Theory plus experiment gives a natural three-person split; the experimental side is arguably shared with other groups (e.g. the Columbia/Dean-related and Harvard efforts) not in the supplied credit, so the configuration is only as good as the listed names.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years old but replicated across many laboratories and extended to related moire systems; the core observations are robust. Timing is early but the impact is already field-defining.
uncertainties: Whether the origin of the superconductivity and the correlated states is settled; the interpretation is still evolving.
Credit for the experiment beyond the single listed experimentalist, which I cannot resolve from the supplied credit alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct observational access to the strong-field region of black holes, a clear and visually decisive discovery with lasting value for tests of gravity and accretion physics. As a black-hole theorist I value that this finally gives empirical clues in a regime long treated only theoretically.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the VLBI technical development and the collaboration, and Moran contributed foundational mm-VLBI work. The EHT is a very large collaboration, so a three-person cap is intrinsically contentious, but the listed trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: The M87* result (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) are independently consistent with general relativity predictions for the shadow size; some interpretive questions about spin and jet launching remain. Recognition would be reasonably timely.
uncertainties: The collaboration is large and many others (e.g. other EHT leaders, instrument builders) made essential contributions.
Image reconstruction choices and model dependence of the inferred parameters have been debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new organizing principle for quantum matter, with an early theory-experiment loop and broad influence on condensed matter and materials physics. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and Hall-type phases, but this is a distinct step.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the Z2 classification and the spin Hall proposal; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, who are not in the supplied credit). That omission is a real attribution problem for a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, with many materials and a mature literature. Timing is appropriate, although the experimental credit is intertwined with the HgTe prediction.
uncertainties: Absence of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the supplied credited names complicates a fair allocation.
Overlap with already-recognised topological work from 2016 may lower priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation and the quantum origin of structure explain horizon, flatness and the primordial fluctuation spectrum, and the nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum measured in the CMB is a striking confirmation of the structure-generation part. It is one of the central ideas of modern cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation, Linde gave new and chaotic inflation, and Mukhanov computed the quantum origin of perturbations. Starobinsky and Sato, among others, also made decisive contributions and are not in the supplied names, so credit is contested. The list also contains two spellings of Guth, which I treat as one person.
assessment.maturity: The CMB confirms the spectrum and flatness, but the inflationary mechanism itself lacks a decisive test (no primordial gravitational waves detected), so the discovery is not as established as an observation. A committee would worry about prematurity.
uncertainties: No direct evidence for the inflaton or primordial tensor modes; alternatives are not definitively excluded.
Priority disputes involving Starobinsky and others outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The LHC and its general-purpose detectors enabled the Higgs discovery and a decade of precision Standard Model tests. The achievement is monumental, but its scientific content is the discovery enabled rather than a new conceptual advance itself.
assessment.attribution: Evans led the accelerator project, while Della Negra and Jenni were founding leaders of CMS and ATLAS respectively. Other leaders (Gianotti, Virdee, Heuer, and many others) are not in the supplied names, so a three-person configuration is a significant simplification of a collective effort.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with the Higgs recognised in 2013 for the theory. Recognising the machine and detectors is plausible and timely, though the 2013 prize partly reduces urgency.
uncertainties: Prize rules and the apportioning of credit across thousands of contributors.
Whether instrumentation credit is judged separate from the Higgs discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation are the theoretical basis for scalable quantum computing, with deep conceptual links to topological order. Importance and originality are high; I note that experimental demonstrations are now appearing.
assessment.attribution: Shor's code and fault-tolerance results, Steane's codes, and Kitaev's toric code and topological fault tolerance are distinct and each decisive. Others (Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Preskill, Aharonov, Ben-Or) are omitted from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: The theory is mathematically established, but its practical vindication in large-scale devices is still ongoing, which argues for patience.
uncertainties: Large contested credit field outside the three supplied names.
Whether a theory-led prize without full experimental realization is premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations are a robust standard ruler that independently confirm cosmic acceleration and provide key constraints on dark energy; the measurements come directly from galaxy surveys and are very much driven by nature rather than speculation.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's SDSS detection and the 2dFGRS detection by Cole, Percival and colleagues were simultaneous and independent in 2005. Peacock and others are also credited in the list; the three-person choice leaves out other 2dFGRS and SDSS team members.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI), though recent DESI hints about evolving dark energy are unresolved. It is partly overshadowed by the 2011 prize for acceleration.
uncertainties: Which survey team deserves primary credit, and the very large collaborations.
Interpretation of DESI results remains open and may alter the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level are a leap in precision measurement, enabling tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and prospective redefinition of the second. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye achieved the record performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori's proposal and Ye's implementation give a clean two-person attribution. Hall and Haensch already received the 2005 prize for the comb, and others (e.g. Ludlow, Hinkley) did key work.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced at several institutions; recognition appears timely because the SI second redefinition is under discussion.
uncertainties: Overlap with recognition for frequency combs and the trapped-ion clock lineage.
Whether the incremental precision improvement over earlier clocks is judged conceptually decisive.
